recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

theorem split_unsound_without_DD :
    SplitStep KDD 0 [[1], [1]] c3a (.ok (splitEff c3a 0 [[1], [1]])) ∧
    ¬ I1 (splitEff c3a 0 [[1], [1]]) ∧
    ¬ ∀ a b p m₁ m₂, a ≠ b → effective (splitEff c3a 0 [[1], [1]]) a p = some m₁ →
      effective (splitEff c3a 0 [[1], [1]]) b p = some m₂ → Compat m₁ m₂ := by
  refine ⟨.ok (by decide), fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩
  · have := h 1 2 ⟨.modify, some 0, [1], .frame 1, true⟩ ⟨.modify, some 0, [1], .frame 1, true⟩ 1
      (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) rfl rfl (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
    exact absurd this.1 (by decide)
  · exact absurd (h 1 2 1 .modify .modify (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)).1 (by decide)

/-- `exitFrame` rejects the exit of a frame whose local is pinned (B4; pass 2: accepted); the
local is unpinned first. -/
example : ExitStep K0 (pinEff c13a 0 true) .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : EndUseStep K0 0 (pinEff c13a 0 true) .reject := .reject (by decide)

/-- A callee cannot release a root authority of its caller (B3): the root is held by the caller
and not exercisable by the callee (pass 2: accepted). The caller releases its own access. -/
example : ReleaseStep 0 (enterEff c13a [] [(none, none, 0)]) .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : ReleaseStep 2 (deriveEff c13a 0 0 .observe)
    (.ok (releaseEff (deriveEff c13a 0 0 .observe) 2)) := .ok (by decide)

/-- Reading the owned storage of a value shared in `Observe` (B2): the root of the storage, a
`Modify` authority held by the value, is exercisable at `Observe`, the mode the read requests
(pass 2: rejected). Writing it is rejected while the value is shared. Frame 1: 0 value, 2 owned
storage. -/

/-- `transfer` (MM-03.3 §3, O4; A5) does not preserve `Inv3` alone (A1): a part with another
owner than its parent (excluded by `WF3`) is not usable while its parent is; a place owned by

    · simp [s] at h; exact .inr ⟨rfl, h.symm⟩

# Tâche : MM-03.3 — jalon 1, passe 3 (clôture : mort des locaux, alloc, droits restants)

## Git
Même branche `formal/access_model_0.1`, à la suite. Pas de merge, pas de PR. Tout sous `formal/`. `Ern/MM02.lean` inchangé. Spec jointe : MM-03.3 v0.2, non copiée ; les arbitrages de la passe 2 (A1–A11) restent en vigueur ; les arbitrages ci-dessous les complètent et font foi.

## Langue
Code, docstrings, commentaires, messages de commit en anglais. Rapport en français.

## Arbitrages (font foi)
B1. `WF3` reçoit deux clauses : deux emplacements racines (sans parent) distincts ont des empreintes disjointes — les relations parent/enfant d'un même arbre ne sont pas concernées ; toute chaîne d'origines d'une autorité couvrant une feuille aboutit à la racine d'autorité de l'emplacement racine de cette feuille. `WF3` reste la bonne formation des états admissibles, distincte de `Inv3` (sûreté) ; les relations restent totales, `WF3` n'apparaît qu'en hypothèse des théorèmes qui en ont besoin, jamais dans les préconditions ; un état mal formé n'a pas pour autant une issue `reject`.
B2. `ExercisableAt s a m` : l'autorité `a` est exerçable au mode `m` ssi `m ≤ a.mode` et (`a` détenue par le cadre courant, ou détenue par un emplacement `p` tel qu'une autorité exerçable au mode `m` ait un mode effectif ≥ `m` sur toute l'empreinte de `p`). Toutes les opérations exigent le mode qu'elles demandent, pas le mode propre de l'autorité.
B3. Droits : `release` exige une autorité détenue par le cadre courant ou exerçable par lui ; `depend` exige `Modify` exerçable sur le résultat ; `unpin` exige le même droit que `pin` (`Modify`).
B4. `ExitPre` : aucune feuille d'un emplacement qui meurt avec le cadre, stockage possédé transitivement compris, n'est épinglée.
B5. `alloc provider owner extent : ok | fail | reject`.
  - `provider` est l'emplacement de la valeur allocateur, distinct de `owner` en général. Exige un droit de mise à jour de ses métadonnées : `Modify` exerçable, ou `writeShared` sur feuilles `SharedMutable`, comme `issue`.
  - `owner` reçoit la possession ; exige `Modify` exerçable sur `owner`.
  - `fail` si `K.Satisfiable provider extent` est faux : état inchangé.
  - `reject` pour toute précondition statique violée.
  - `ok` : nouvelle racine d'identité fraîche, possédée par `owner`, feuilles `Uninit`, racine d'autorité `Modify` détenue par `owner`.
  - L'échec défini appartient au contrat de l'allocateur ; il n'ajoute rien à `AllocStep` de MM-02. Les cas qui modélisaient `alloc` par un local d'entrée sont réécrits avec `alloc`.
B6. `free` refuse toute feuille épinglée, statiquement (`K.Pinned`) ou dynamiquement, sans exception. La fin des obligations externes passe exclusivement par `unpin` sous `ExternalDone`. Aucun état d'épinglage ne peut survivre à une libération.
B7. Non-échappement (O4.6) lu dans l'état d'arrivée : le cadre de chaque ancre est celui qu'elle aura après le transfert.
B8. Invariant `AnchorOrder` : tout emplacement utilisable dépend d'ancres détenues dans un cadre au plus aussi ancien que le sien. `transfer` le préserve en rejetant un déplacement qui emmènerait une ancre dans un cadre plus jeune qu'un de ses dépendants utilisables. Ajouté à `Inv3`.
B9. `K.Invalidates` retiré.
B10. Lectures confirmées de la passe 2 : portée étendue de `endUse`/`free` ((c) 9, 10) ; utilisabilité lue après l'effet ; ancres d'un conteneur ne suivant pas une partie transférée ; `Modify` pour `pin` et pour la destination de `issue` ; `auth` opaque pour `free`.

## Étapes (un commit par étape)
1. B1, B8 : clauses de `WF3`, `AnchorOrder` dans `Inv3`, préservation par toutes les opérations.
2. **`exitFrame_no_dangling`** : sous `WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s`, après `exitFrame`, aucune autorité active ne couvre une feuille d'un emplacement non utilisable — locaux du cadre sorti, stockage qu'ils possèdent transitivement, et quelles que soient les autorités conservées par transferts et ré-ancrages. Énoncé sur les feuilles, pas sur le détenteur des autorités. C'est le théorème de clôture du jalon ; s'il ne se prouve pas, le rapport dit exactement quelle clause manque, avec contre-exemple ; l'énoncé n'est jamais affaibli.
3. B2, B3 : `ExercisableAt`, droits de `release`, `depend`, `unpin` ; `exercise_requires_hold` réénoncé par mode. Témoin : lecture du stockage possédé d'une valeur partagée en `Observe` → `ok`.
4. B4 à B7, B9 : `ExitPre`, `alloc`, `free`, non-échappement, retrait. Théorèmes `alloc_fresh`, `alloc_preserves`, `alloc_owned_root`, `alloc_fail_unchanged`, `free_no_pin` (après `free`, aucune feuille libérée n'est épinglée).
5. Cas : les 34 rejoués ; plus :
   - local épinglé à la sortie → `reject` ;
   - `release` par l'appelé d'une racine de l'appelant → `reject` ;
   - `depend` sur un emplacement de l'appelant sans droit → `reject` ;
   - valeur ancrée sur la racine de son propre stockage rendue à l'appelant → `ok` ;
   - `transfer` emmenant une ancre dans un cadre plus jeune qu'un dépendant → `reject` au `transfer` ;
   - `alloc` en milieu de cadre, fournisseur distinct du propriétaire, puis `free` → `ok` ;
   - `alloc` non satisfiable → `fail`, état inchangé ; `alloc` sans droit sur le fournisseur → `reject` ;
   - `free` d'une feuille épinglée → `reject` ; `unpin` sous `ExternalDone` puis `free` → `ok`.

## Hors périmètre
Jalon 2, concurrence, handles, `defer`, obligation de libération, syntaxe.

## Règles
Zéro `sorry` ; `#print axioms` au plus {propext, Quot.sound} ; aucun `noncomputable` ; `lake build` sans avertissement ; docstrings citant la clause ou l'arbitrage ; rien d'inventé ; aucun énoncé affaibli, tout changement justifié ; revue adverse comme en passe 2 ; contre-exemples adverses conservés.

## Livrable
Module commité ; `formal/reports/MM03_v0.1_p3.md` : sections (a)–(l) comme en passe 2, plus (m) statut de `exitFrame_no_dangling` et liste des clauses de `WF3` et `Inv3` qu'il utilise.

|---|---|
| `lake build` | réussit, sans avertissement |

Pour garder les axiomes dans cet ensemble, `OwnedIn` reçoit une instance `Decidable` tirée de `ownedWithin_iff`. Sans elle, un `by_cases` sur `OwnedIn` passait par `Classical.choice`.

## Résultats principaux

1. **`exitFrame_no_dangling` est prouvé sous `WF3`**, sans `Inv3` (`exitFrame_no_dangling`). Après la sortie, aucune autorité active ne couvre une feuille d'un emplacement du cadre sorti : ses locaux et leur stockage possédé, transitivement. La preuve utilise une clause de `WF3` que la passe 2 avait omise : A4, « Une racine reste détenue par le propriétaire de son emplacement », condition de possession que A1 range dans `WF3` (`RootHeld`). Sans cette clause, l'énoncé est faux : `exitFrame_no_dangling_needs_rootHeld`. Détail en (m).

Conséquence : `reachable_access_invariant_underDD` conclut `WF3 ∧ Inv3base`, c'est-à-dire I1 à I4, et non `Inv3`. Voir (d) 1 et (e) 2.
3. **La phrase de B8 se contredit.** « détenues dans un cadre au plus aussi ancien que le sien » s'oppose à la phrase suivante, qui rejette le déplacement d'une ancre vers un cadre plus jeune qu'un dépendant. structure K where
  DeclaredDisjoint : List Nat → List Nat → Prop
  SharedMutable : Nat → Prop
  Pinned : Nat → Prop
  ExternalDone : Nat → Prop
  Deallocable : Nat → Prop
  FreeCompat : Nat → Nat → Prop
  Satisfiable : Nat → Nat → Prop

/-- Obligation of `DeclaredDisjoint` (MM-03.3.8): a declaration never covers two regions that
really overlap. -/
def DDSound (k : K) : Prop := ∀ r r', k.DeclaredDisjoint r r' → ∀ l ∈ r, l ∉ r'

/-- Initial state: one frame, no place, no authority. -/
def S3.init : S3 :=
  ⟨[0], 1, [], fun _ => .uninit, [], fun _ => [], fun _ => false, fun _ => false, fun _ => false⟩

/-- `origin` link of the authority with index `i` (MM-03.3.4). -/
def S3.org (s : S3) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (s.A[i]?).bind (·.origin)

/-- Strict ancestors of authority `i` along `origin`: `i` descends from each (MM-03.3.5). -/
def S3.ancs (s : S3) (i : Nat) : List Nat := chain s.org i

def S3.Active (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Prop := ∃ y, s.A[x]? = some y ∧ y.active = true

instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Decidable (s.Active x) :=
  match h : s.A[x]? with
  | some y => if hy : y.active = true then isTrue ⟨y, h, hy⟩
    else isFalse fun ⟨y', h', hy'⟩ => by rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact hy hy'
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨_, h', _⟩ => by rw [h] at h'; cases h'

/-- Current frame: the head of the stack (MM-03.3.1). -/
def S3.top (s : S3) : Nat := s.F.headD 0

/-! ## Decidable helpers -/

/-- Predicate on an optional value: `P y` for `some y`, `d` for `none`. -/
def OptP {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) : Prop :=
  match o with
  | some y => P y
  | none => d

instance {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) [DecidablePred P] [Decidable d] :
    Decidable (OptP o P d) :=
  match o with
  | some y => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (P y))
  | none => inferInstanceAs (Decidable d)

satisfiable. -/
def KT (sh pinned done dealloc : List Nat) (compat : List (Nat × Nat)) : K :=

      heldIn s.P p y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

instance (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAccessOK s p j) := by
  unfold EndUseAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Anchor `x` survives the end of the value at `p` (A6): not held within `p`, not the root of
`p`, with a holder that stays live. -/
def EndUseAnchorOK (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P p y.holder ∧ ¬ IsRootOf s p y ∧
    HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold EndUseAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `endUse p` (A6). Usability of the anchored places is read after the end:
a place that dies with `p` has no usable dependent afterwards. In order: `p` usable;
exercisable `Modify` on `p` (A2);
no active derived authority on an ending leaf, or descending from an authority that the end
releases (MM-03.3 §3, O3.2), held elsewhere than in `p` and staying live; no
usable place anchored on an authority held by `p`, on its root, or held by a holder that dies;
no ending leaf pinned (dynamically, A8, or statically, `Pinned`) without `ExternalDone`. The
ending leaves include those of the owned places, which die (A6). -/
def EndUsePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, EndUseAccessOK s p j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q,
    EndUseAnchorOK s p x) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → (s.pin l = true ∨ k.Pinned l) →
    k.ExternalDone l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] (s : S3) (p : Nat) :
    Decidable (EndUsePre k s p) := by
  unfold EndUsePre; infer_instance

/-- `endUse` as a relation (A6). -/


/-- Anchor `x` survives the release of `p` (A6): it covers no leaf of `p`, is not held within
`p`, and its holder stays live. -/
def FreeAnchorOK (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P p) ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P p y.holder ∧
    HolderLive (freeS s p) y.holder) True

instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (FreeAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold FreeAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `free p auth` (A6), in order: `p` deallocable by the allocator contract
(`Deallocable`) and `auth` a compatible deallocation authority (`FreeCompat`, MM-03.3.8); `p` a
usable owned root (a part is not a unit of storage, and `WF3` gives a part the `dead` flag of its
parent); exercisable `Modify` on `p` (B2); no active derived authority on a freed leaf, or
descending from a deactivated authority, held elsewhere and staying live; no usable place
anchored on an authority covering `p`, held within `p`, or whose holder dies; no freed leaf
pinned, statically (`Pinned`) or dynamically, without exception (B6: external obligations end
only through `unpin` under `ExternalDone`). -/
def FreePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) : Prop :=
  k.Deallocable p ∧ k.FreeCompat p auth ∧ s.Usable p ∧ OwnedRoot s p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, FreeAccessOK s p j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (freeS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (freeS s p).D q,
    FreeAnchorOK s p x) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, FreedLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned]
    [DecidablePred k.Deallocable] [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) :
    Decidable (FreePre k s p auth) := by
  unfold FreePre; infer_instance

/-- `free` as a relation (A6). -/
def FreeStep (k : K) (p auth : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (FreePre k s p auth) (freeEff s p)

Inchangé (passe 2, (k)). `DDSound k` est aussi une hypothèse de `exitFrame_no_dangling_reachable`, qui passe par `reachable_access_invariant_underDD`.

### `SharedMutable`

Inchangé, avec un usage de plus : le droit du fournisseur de `alloc` peut être un droit `writeShared` sur ses feuilles (`ProviderRight`). Les théorèmes sur `alloc` ne supposent rien de ce contrat.

### `Pinned` (statique) et épinglage dynamique

- **Obligation.** Inchangée (I5).
- **Démontré pour tout `K`.**

- **Obligation.** Inchangée.
- **Usage.** `unpin` (B3 exige en plus le droit de `pin`) et l'exception de `endUse` (A8). B6 en fait la seule fin des obligations externes pour `free` ; pour `endUse`, question (e) 9. B4 n'en prévoit aucune pour la sortie.

### `Invalidates`

Retiré de `K` (B9).
